title: Chilam Balam Texts, vol. 1: Chumayel, Calkiní, Libro de los Médicos
shelf_note: 19th-century hand copy of the Chilam Balam of Chumayel (Yucatec Maya prophetic/calendrical text); a genuine primary source, though the book carries no collection or tradition tag.
structure_note: printed_repeats 109 is explained by the leaf numbering: rectos carry a blue ink number (22 on p45, 23 on p47) and versos repeat it in pencil (22 on p46), plus a second pencil series (25, 26). Not a defect. 70 of 294 pages untranslated.

first words of the page left in Maya; meta claims the previous page ended '...and was seated: Kan', which I could not verify

ocr_errors.image: '26' is a later pencil numeral written into the gap in the line
ocr_errors.problem: later-hand foliation read as part of the text

tr_errors.problem: pencil folio number translated as a numeral in the prophecy

other.note: the OCR's <meta>, <warning> and <unclear>faint pencil note</unclear> block (a description of the scan) is copied verbatim to the top of the translation

ocr_errors.ocr: çatal u naat çicnal u yum çicnal u naa
ocr_errors.image: çatal u naat yicnal u yum yicnal u naa
ocr_errors.problem: yicnal ('beside') misread as çicnal; the translation still gives 'beside'
x read as t; the translation 'bandaged' follows kaxan anyway

book_verdict: A clean, careful transcription of a hard cursive Maya manuscript, with a literal translation that holds up. The one real slip is the pencil folio '26' read and translated as part of the text on p46.

title: 儒林外史(二十): The Scholars, vol 20
shelf_note: Wu Jingzi's 18th-century novel in a woodblock edition (ch. 55). Shelved only in the generic 'universallibrary' collection, which is fine, but it lies outside the library's core esoteric/early-science traditions.

other.note: OCR tag <script>handwritten</script> on a woodblock-printed page

ocr_errors.image: 第五十五回 in the block margin (chapter 55), with leaf number 五
ocr_errors.problem: margin chapter label transcribed as running text, not tagged as furniture
misread; the translation still says 'for his livelihood'

tr_errors.problem: the margin label means chapter 55, not page 55; a false page number appears in the reader text

ocr_errors.problem: 四 'four' misread as 西; the translation drops the number of benches

book_verdict: An accurate OCR and a fluent, faithful translation of The Scholars, ch. 55. The only things a reader would notice are the margin chapter label rendered as 'Page 55' and the wrong 'handwritten' tag.

title: 易原·卷四~卷五 (vol 2)
shelf_note: Cheng Dachang's Yi yuan, a Song Yijing treatise, in the Siku Quanshu manuscript copy (欽定四庫全書 in the margin). Correct for a Yijing/cosmology shelf.
structure_note: Only 4 printed numbers detected. The Siku leaves carry folio numbers in the centre fold, mostly cut off at the frame edge, so the low count is expected. 3 of 122 pages untranslated.

tr_errors.english: Meng Jingyi <note>Meng Yi, a fourth-century Jin dynasty scholar</note>
tr_errors.problem: the note adds an unsupported alternative name and date (Meng Jingyi is usually placed in Southern Qi); invented gloss

tr_errors.english: Qian and Kun <note>Heaven and Earth, the two primary hexagrams</note>
tr_errors.problem: in the context of the six children these are trigrams, not hexagrams

tr_errors.source: 故信善美大自二中四下者積而上之
tr_errors.english: from the two central qualities of trustworthiness and goodness down to beauty and greatness, one accumulates upward
tr_errors.problem: '自二中四下' (from the second ... the four below) is forced into a reading the source does not clearly give; the Mencius note is reasonable

book_verdict: An excellent OCR of a clean Siku manuscript copy, with a careful translation. One invented biographical note on Meng Jingyi.

title: 儒林外史(十六): The Scholars, vol 16
shelf_note: Wu Jingzi's novel (ch. 42, the examination-ghost story), the same edition as slot 2. Generic 'universallibrary' shelf, outside the core traditions.

other.note: OCR tag <script>handwritten</script> on a woodblock print

title: 三易備遺·卷六~卷十 (vol 7)
shelf_note: Zhu Yuansheng's San Yi bei yi (Song Yijing numerology: Lianshan, Guicang, Zhouyi), Siku Quanshu copy. Fits a Yijing/cosmology shelf.
structure_note: p92 is a chapter-end leaf with two lines of text and blank columns, correctly transcribed as short. The single backstep is probably a misread centre-fold folio. 17 of 216 pages untranslated.

tr_errors.source: 為周易之六六則之 | (p92) 河圖乾坤縱而六子衡也
tr_errors.english: becomes the principle of six-by-six pairs in the Zhouyi. | (p92) In the Hetu, Qian and Kun are vertical
tr_errors.problem: the closing '則之' ('takes as its model [the Hetu]') runs across the page break and is dropped, so the link between the 6x6 scheme and the Hetu is lost

book_verdict: An accurate OCR and a faithful, well-glossed translation. The only issue is a small seam loss of '則之' across the page break between p91 and p92.
